assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single polymers one monomer at a time through a molecular-scale pore rests on a clear physical principle: ionic current blockade as a molecular-resolution transduction. It created a genuinely new capability, portable long-read single-molecule sequencing, and the measurement sits at the border of physics, chemistry and biology that I find most compelling. The impact is unforeseen-in-1990 and now broad (genomics, clinical and field sequencing, protein sensing).
assessment.attribution: Deamer and Branton conceived translocation of nucleic acids through a pore, Kasianowicz demonstrated it with alpha-hemolysin, Bayley engineered protein pores with single-base sensitivity, and Akeson showed enzyme-ratcheted, controlled single-nucleotide stepping. A three-person configuration of conception (Deamer), pore engineering (Bayley) and motor-controlled reading (Akeson) is defensible, but the Kasianowicz and Branton claims make allocation genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Mature: commercial devices have been used for over a decade, with independent confirmation and steady accuracy improvements. Timing is good given the field is established but still advancing.
uncertainties: Competing claims from Branton and Kasianowicz for the founding experiments could undermine a three-name citation.
I cannot independently verify each person's exact priority dates or whether living status limits the configuration.
Part of the sequencing impact may be viewed as genomics or physics rather than chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Unifying electronic-structure calculation and molecular dynamics in a single extended Lagrangian made ab initio dynamics practical for liquids, solids and reactions. The idea is elegant and principle-based, and it opened a vast class of problems (water, phase transitions, reactive processes) that were previously inaccessible. It is also widely used, which suits my emphasis on generative potential.
assessment.attribution: The 1985 paper is cleanly attributable to exactly two people, which gives a simple and defensible citation. Parrinello's other contributions (metadynamics, ML potentials) are separate and need not be bundled in.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: forty years of independent use and verification. Possible drawback is that recognition is arguably late rather than premature, and Chemistry 2013 honoured related multiscale modelling, which a committee may feel overlaps.
uncertainties: Overlap in the committee's mind with the 2013 computational chemistry prize.
Some of the practical impact depends on later DFT functional development not credited here.
Whether the committee prefers to couple this with Parrinello's later work is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Converting one base to another without double-strand breaks, using a programmable deaminase fused to a Cas protein, is a new chemical capability on DNA at single-nucleotide resolution. The principle is simple, the results quantitative, and the therapeutic and research potential vast. It builds on a prize-recognised tool (CRISPR, 2020), so the originality of the extension must be weighed.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the conceptual design and the engineering of cytosine and adenine base editors; Komor and Gaudelli were the lead authors of the key papers. A single-name prize to Liu is the cleanest, but two-trainee credit would be unusual for the committee, and the Komor and Gaudelli contributions are real.
assessment.maturity: Fairly early for a prize, but clinical trials and base-editing therapies have shown human proof of concept, and the independent adoption is extensive.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as a refinement of CRISPR recognised in 2020.
Clinical outcomes are still maturing.
Allocation among Liu, Komor and Gaudelli is unresolved; Nishida and Kondo's parallel work (credited in the longlist) complicates it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organising principle in cells is a physical-chemistry concept (condensate thermodynamics, multivalency, material properties) with strong quantitative grounding and broad reach in biology and disease. It changed how cellular compartmentalisation is thought about, an unforeseen capability for explanation.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne demonstrated liquid-like P granules in 2009; Rosen demonstrated multivalent-interaction-driven phase separation in a reconstituted system in 2012. These three give a natural triad; Pappu and Mittag are theoretical and biophysical contributors who would be excluded.
assessment.maturity: Strong confirmation of the concept but substantial ongoing debate over which cellular structures are truly phase separated and what functional role it has, so the interpretation is not yet stable.
uncertainties: Debate over the physiological relevance versus in vitro artefacts.
Whether this is chemistry or cell biology.
Exclusion of Pappu and Mittag could be seen as unfair.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Using a bifunctional or molecular-glue small molecule to hijack the ubiquitin ligase machinery and destroy a target is a new pharmacological paradigm that expands the druggable proteome. The idea is clear and chemically driven, and the impact on medicinal chemistry is large with many compounds in clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies founded the PROTAC concept (2001), Ciulli contributed structure-based design and VHL-based degraders, and Handa and Ito identified cereblon as the thalidomide target. A trio is plausible but credit among PROTAC and molecular-glue pioneers is spread out.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is still emerging, with several phase 3 trials ongoing; the concept is confirmed but approvals are lacking so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: No approved PROTAC drug yet.
The molecular glue history (thalidomide) differs from the PROTAC history and may need separate recognition.
Choice among Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Handa and Ito is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites reached high solar-cell efficiencies in a decade, approaching physical limits, with remarkable defect tolerance and a clear materials-chemistry story. It is a striking case of new capability and rapid translation, with quantitative benchmarking against the Shockley-Queisser limit.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitised cell, Park and Grätzel's group and Snaith's group drove efficiency and stability gains. Allocation is crowded with many credible names, so any three people leave out significant contributors.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency is high but long-term stability and scale-up are unresolved; the field is moving fast, so recognition may be premature.
uncertainties: Long-term stability and lead toxicity are not resolved.
Priority and credit contested among six candidates.
The physics community may see this as materials physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Folding DNA into arbitrary designed shapes by programmed base pairing created a general bottom-up route to nanostructures with molecular precision, with uses ranging from nanophotonics to molecular machines. The principle is simple and the capability new and generative.
assessment.attribution: Rothemund's 2006 origami paper is the decisive contribution; Shih extended to three dimensions and Yin to tile-based assembly. Seeman founded the field but I understand he is deceased, so he cannot be credited and is not in the list.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and widely used, but real-world applications are still emerging, so the timing is acceptable but not pressing.
uncertainties: Uncertain how the committee will weigh impact against the 2016 molecular machines prize.
Credit division between origami and tile approaches.
Seeman's deceased status means foundational credit cannot be recognised.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Single-molecule FRET allows measuring distances and dynamics of individual biomolecules, giving access to heterogeneity and kinetics hidden in ensembles. It is physical and quantitative, and it enabled mechanistic insight on folding and enzymes.
assessment.attribution: Weiss, Ha and Zhuang each contributed early demonstrations and methods in the 1990s; the allocation is a plausible trio, though Selvin and others contributed too.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely used; but 2014 recognised super-resolution microscopy, so the committee may consider the single-molecule field recently honoured.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2014 prize in the committee's mind.
Whether the contribution is a method refinement of fluorescence spectroscopy.
Credit among Weiss, Ha, Zhuang and Selvin is uncertain.
